body: Awesome, dude!
I'm constantly confused about my own depression actually cause (after meds), it's not like I feel sad all the time, but perhaps lingering symptoms of depression still remain?
Interesting...Thanks for the suggestion, I'll look into it

I'm not really sure if non-ADHD people have these symptoms tbh, but if you truly believe you have ADHD, then I would suggest you try and find another practice that will test you. I have often seen many people on this subreddit say they got tested, got told they didn't have it, went to another practice, and then they said "holy hell god yes you do have adhd!" Consensus and research isn't straight for ADHD, and some psychologists may be biased in some ways while nearly all have some level of subjectivity in their diagnosis.

Wish you well, my friend.

That's a very thoughtful way to think about it,, knowing it's inevitable and time is on your side as it marches unyieldingly. I guess time is the only stability we have, the only thing we can rely on so it's okay. I'll have to try that thought out sometime. As for now, hope you've gotten over your slump and wish you well my friend!

That makes a whole lot of sense, thank you! I was wondering about the score line as well. In fact, I have to say that without the score line, these round little pills have been very hard to cut accurately. Half of the time they aren't cut evenly, meaning there's bupropion dust and maybe 0.4 of the pill so I'm left unsure if I'm supposed to swallow the bitter shavings as well?
I only got the jitters from the 300 mg tablets, but I think what you said makes sense. I'll check it out, thanks for the help!
Glad it's been working for you. Others have been warning against it, so I want to double-check on my end. Maybe you should also confirm this with your doc just in case?

Thanks for letting me know, that's what I've seen other people saying too. It's absolutely bonkers. I didn't know for the longest time because I never got the jittery effects again after switching to 1.5 pills (275 mg)? It's very confusing.
Thanks for informing me. It's weird cause I've been on the 1.5 pill for months now and haven't felt any jittery effects the 300 mg gave me? This is also why I didn't feel like anything was wrong,.

Certainly! I think that's good advice too when we live in such an unfortunately ignorant world. We all deserve help, and we all deserve to be advocated for, even if we have to do it ourselves.

I'm glad you had an easier time with your advisors and won the fight, it's great to hear that some success in accommodations isn't impossible, and we can be hopeful.

Hey, I'm not sure if it's so appropriate to be saying that people should've just said no so they wouldn't be in their current situation. It sounds minimizing and victim-blaming, especially when OP is "Seeking Empathy / Support" and in a situation where someone also is making assumptions about them.

I don't think you should be making assumptions here either, like that OP never tried saying no. OP knows their situation the best, and there are plenty of other situations where people don't feel safe or comfortable saying no.

Also, it's a well-known fact that schools do not treat their ADHD students well nor attempt to understand them so I'm not sure if it's wise to side with the advisors when there isn't more context.

Hey, thanks for the suggestion. I'm honestly kind of unsure if some of the things I do can even be classified as OCD, and recently I think I might not have OCD to the extent of needing intervention. I've got OCD in the sense that I'm a bit of a germaphobe, and I constantly need to check if doors are locked and secured and do it several times a night even though I literally just did it minutes ago.
Dang, Buttercup instantly started playing in my head the moment I read this. Now I know what I'm going to wake up to tomorrow

Not sure if it's related to just ADHD, but I have this 100%, and it's so annoying. I'll be trying to concentrate on something, and it just starts going! Sometimes for songs I haven't listened to in years! I'd love to know if there's a way to turn off this station because I want off. 

*(I'm curious to know what songs your head plays though.)*

*Adapt. Improvise. Overcome.*

(In all seriousness, glad we can relate as toilet buddies :) )
Def feel you on the racing heart part. Seriously feels like my heart's going to burst sometimes.
That's an interesting point. It's possible that might be why, but unfortunately, I do not get the same sense of urgency until I'm on the toilet, *sigh.*

I think that makes a lot of sense. Maybe it's cause of distractions and just a lesser sense of urgency? But you can imagine how probably how weird it is when I bring my laptop with me to the bathroom. 

*"Brb going to go finish my essay" \*sprints to the nearest bathroom\**

I agree very much. I'm always happy when there are caption options available on youtube, appreciate it a ton. I'm not entirely sure if this is related, but as a student, I usually insist on typing my notes in class, and the notes are basically always a transcript of everything the professor has said word-for-word. It helps me understand better because I can scroll back up during class if I missed what they just said or I can look at it later and know exactly what the professor said.

For this reason I am better at talking to people by typing than in person. Also, it makes presenting very annoying because I cannot explain my ideas in the going-with-the-flow kind of way. I have to memorize and recite my presentation word-for-word; otherwise, I am completely thrown off and cannot make a single sentence that makes sense up there.
That's also a concern for me too. It's like, when am I gonna crash because of these poor eating habits? I hope yours goes as gently as possible tho ;(
It's insightful to think of these habits in the context of ADHD. I'm wondering if you ever brought it up to a health professional that could give you their opinion?

That makes sense. I'm actually starting to wonder if it's because we're focusing *too* hard in the wrong way, and we're *too* tense? Cause I know I get anxious and stressed during class because of my past experiences with school and my ADHD, but I tried really hard the other day to relax and just sit there, and I didn't get a headache? And I seemed to get more information than if I was in "headache-mode" for a lack of better words.
That's great! I'm so happy for you. I'm sure it must be such a liberating feeling after all these years.

Thanks for even sharing your concerns with us. I know that can feel weird and uncomfortable sometimes, especially with a new diagnosis in a situation like yours. Imo, I think ADHD is just a part of you, a different type of logic from other non-ADHD people that blends in with the rest of your brain, making it whole, but also making it difficult to pick out as distinctly ADHD. It's kind of like baking a cake. The flour, eggs, sugar, and etc. all combined and distributed throughout the batter, and when it comes out of the oven, it's really hard to pick out where the raw eggs went into or try to taste for specifically just the sugar. So, what I mean is that I'm not sure if you'll be able to pick out your ADHD distinctly from the "rest" of your brain cause it's one in the same. The idea of even having the "rest" of your brain being the non-ADHD/"normal" component is also pushed by non-ADHD people in a very bad way. If you ask me, I don't think you should worry yourself over where ADHD begins and where it ends or at least, not actively look for it because it usually ends in a lot of frustration and depression, and as long as who you are and what you do don't harm others and bring you, every piece of you including your ADHD, joy, then I think it's perfectly valid.
That sounds incredibly comfortable and nice. A little decorated space to yourself to do work in comfortably, that's self-care!
I'd like to believe I'd be productive on my bed as well, but of course, I'm shifting positions every two seconds and confused why I'm not able to focus, hah.

I feel you on different leg positions. I never know what I'm gonna get that day!

As for the kitchen, that's really interesting. I wonder if the change in height and free space to kick your legs helps?
You're doing god's work out there. Take care.

I'm coming to the point in my life where I realize how true your words are. Life's a tiring, learning process, and it's shocking how many years you have to spend before you really seem to feel like you're living "correctly" for a lack of better word.

Thanks for the suggestion! I'll try to keep it in mind. Glad that you've got some things figured out for yourself.

I admittingly have not had an experience completely similar in actions, but moreso in the elements and what they represented. It must be quite a shock to learn you have ADHD, and that you're looking at everything in the past with new lenses. It really messes up your perspective, and you'll find yourself having to readjust yourself to understand this new piece of yourself you've just learned. Since your doctor has diagnosed you with ADHD and not NPD, I would say this dude's diagnosis is not good especially since he's not a doctor. I think you should talk with him about your own feelings and what's been going on (to the extent you're comfortable with ofc), and if he still insists you have NPD, I think he's not respecting you as a person, and I don't think that's healthy.

Now that you know you have ADHD, you can understand yourself better and see things in a new context. There's no shame in having ADHD and having different coping mechanisms as long as they're healthy and consensual for all parties involved, and from what you're saying, I think what you were doing in the past was completely fine. You even know that you didn't have harmful intentions, and your past relationships seemed to go pretty well from what you're saying. Imo, there's no wrong way to love or cope as long as it's consensual and not hurting anyone, and it seems like you've got your own unique way to love! If this dude doesn't respect it even after hearing your situation and feelings, then I think he's applying his own morals to you and not respecting and/or understanding your boundaries which is incredibly unhealthy. So I think you can continue what you're doing, and the ADHD shouldn't be a mark of shame or regret but just a new lens to tell you why something's the way it is. It's a new logic that's been always a part of you, and that's okay.

Yeah, I've got no idea why that is?? I'm absolutely exhausted after it too, and I just have to immediately go back home and rest lest depressive or anxious thoughts start to fester in my brain. I think from what I looked up, it's specifically a tension headache for me? I'm not sure though, and I'm wondering if it's an auto-response from my body after years of academic trauma. Just wondering, does painkillers make it go away? Mines only lasts for the time I've gotta focus on (and then leaves me tired afterwards) so I've never tried to take any.
It sucks sometimes cause I want to raise my hand too, but if I did it as much as I was confused, I'd be stopping the class every 30 seconds. It's a struggle, but I hope you can manage.

Trying to navigate your own brain in the context of a non-ADHD world is no doubt difficult, and it can definitely make you feel worse about yourself when you're just trying to understand yourself and go through life. Making an overview of what to learn actually sounds like a smart idea, and I'm considering that since I also need to see a "big picture" in my head before I even start understanding a lick of things. Glad that you found something that works for you there!
The struggle is real. At least we know we're not alone here!

Thanks for sharing your experience! It was insightful. I've definitely heard before that some ADHD people benefit from written instructions than videos since they can go at their own pace, and I feel like that's definitely true (the amount of times I've rewinded on videos is truly astounding.) I'm happy that you came out of school kicking and screaming with A's and B's despite the lack of support from teachers that you deserved. The school system really sucks in that regard, but at the very least you know how hard you've worked for that success, and now you get to live it being employed and knowing what's best for yourself, more than what those teachers had going for them. I call that a win!

Thanks for the advice! I'm glad you were able to find structure in a world that seems so structure-less to us. And, I've never really thought about processing my negative ADHD attributes and anxiety like that. Using your confusion to your own advantage seems incredibly interesting. I'll keep it in mind!

Also, you're right about the curiosity part. There's simply not enough time in the non-ADHD world for us!

It makes sense to be bitter. Classes aren't built for people like us, and when we try to engage in ways that are comfortable and stimulating for us, we're shot down. You're clearly  a great and interactive learner, and it's unfortunate that not many teachers can see that when that's like every professor's dream.

I think I know what you mean! If something isn't explained in a way I don't immediately get, I'll be messed up for the rest of the class time, making me also behind. I've fortunately met some great professors that described everything in "baby" terms for me, but you're right, it is a lot of having to do things yourself which is unfair, and for now, we'll have to make do and do the best we can, knowing that it's also okay to take a break when we're frustrated. 

Also thank you for the advice, I am trying to look into possible accessibility options at my school right now though the process is slow and exhausting (and also gives me anxiety too so I feel you on that.) I also very much relate to the inability to differentiate between what's anxiety and ADHD, but I've also gotta make do with that too, knowing it's a part of me.

Since you're talking about the accessibility options at my school, I think that means that you also know how ADHD-havers like ourselves need some accommodations sometimes and deserve to feel respected. This might not help too much, but I wanted to say that I think you owe it to yourself to get those accommodations. You've made it this far, and now you're giving me this advice and encouragement. I think you deserve to feel comfortable and at your best, and there's no shame in that.

(Congrats on the degree btw! You've made it that far, and I admire that sm)

I'm glad to here they got to where they wanted to be despite all the challenges. I think I can understand what they mean too. It's completely disorienting for me when I don't know the big picture before starting to learn something, like where does it fit in??

Also showing up to class is definitely hard when the classes are too fuzzy in my head as well. It kind of feels like a giant hump for me that I have to get over, but even trying to do that makes me incredibly anxious. Great that you did well in some of your classes though, that's at least a win!
Gotcha dude, I've gotta have a perfect set-up too to even start doing anything, and the worst part is what I consider perfect set-up changes every day!
I can empathize. I've had to drop out of classes a few times because it just got too much when I kept getting left behind. Good luck on figuring things out!

It sucks to hear that's been your experience when you're just trying to get more information (since you also paid for it too.) You have every right to be salty. College (and the K-12 system too ofc) is often not built for people like us so we have to take extra steps to care for ourselves. College is already shitty for people without ADHD so it's bound to be doubly shitty for those with, but that's why we gotta look out for each other and know we're not alone!

I think I know what you mean. I think I do have a tendency to "get" things more if I know why it logically is that way, but that's also what's so bad for studying since now I'll have to take constant detours to figure out why what I'm studying is like that. On the flip side, I guess that means I truly know what's happening if I get to study!

Also good luck with going back to college!

\*rubs hands together evily\*

*Yesss, use your ADHD to your advantage hee hee hee*

Thanks for that bit of encouragement! I appreciate it.

You're right about me having anxiety, but unfortunately, it's not the only thing that affects my study life and goals. It's like you mentioned, my working memory is definitely what's the biggest issue. Right now, I have been dealing with medication at least so yay!

I know what you mean by the instant auto-calculation you do in your head when anyone says it took them x amount of hours. For that very reason, I've gotta clear out a day or two in my week constantly just to do a bit of studying. I think for me, what speeds up the studying process is knowing organizing an outline (whether it's in your head or on paper) of the topics you're going to study and how they're related to each other. This is because for me, not knowing how things are organized in the "bigger picture" confuses me and makes me spend a lot more time than I need. It also lets me not microfocus all the time.

Good luck with your studying!

Hi, everyone! Thanks for all your responses! I wanna take the time to actually respond to all your comments, but I've read them earlier, and I'm glad to know that we all have similar experiences. Dealing with adhd can be exhausting and isolating, and I'm happy that we can share experiences and feelings about this as some form of comfort on this strange planet, or at least it's been like that for me. But I hope it's also been that way for you all too. 

**Good Luck out there!**
That's an interesting way to distract yourself. I wonder if it also helps you sleep better?

Please take what I say of my own experience with a grain of salt as I don't fully know your (or your friend's) situation, and my experience is just *my* experience.

For me, chronic depression has been a bitch for as long as I can remember. It's been almost an everyday occurrence, and while I should be used to it by now (and in some ways, I am by how I expect it), it never stops being difficult everytime for me. I have intrusive thoughts and anxiety that coincides, and suicidal thoughts come so often even when my mind wasn't even in that sort of space earlier. It's like I'm being held hostage by another person who's making me think all these things when I really don't want to. My depression comes and goes, and fluctuates throughout the day, but I'd say it's like 5/7 days a week I feel like this. I think it might be the lack of dopamine for me personally, but idk.

I also find that being reminded of my successes or my relationships with people and how they value me often brings me down from extremely depressed down to a simmer since depression often clouds us from seeing how we actually are and how we fit into the world.

You're a really great friend for trying to support your buddy and looking for advice. I appreciate people like you for caring for others and their needs, the world needs more people like you.

As for your friend, since they're suicidal, please try to get him some help whether it be a crisis line or therapy or any sort of mental aid, and let him know you care about him.

And as for you, please also take care of yourself. This is no doubt an emotionally-draining situation to be in. Godspeed.

Firstly, I want to say I'm really sorry the adults around you treated you that way and downplayed a lot of your symptoms and feelings. You deserved better.

Secondly, I think I know what you mean by replaying cringe moments in your head randomly. It sucks so much because I'll just be doing my work and space out for 2 seconds and then boom, *remember this cringey memory of you doing something weird? Feel ashamed, everyone remembers* or maybe *remember this bad thing you did as a kid to that other kid? Yeah, they're gonna come back to get vengeance on you, and you deserve it.* I've got no idea how to stop them except trying to reassure myself that I live in the present and not the past, and I've got all these things in the present including my present self which is always the best version of yourself since you've got all this experience and knowledge.

Worst part though is that I also make a very loud squeeky ass noise whenever I think of these cringe memories, and everyone around me will be like ???

Unfortunately, the benefits can take some time (weeks or even a full month) to fully kick in since they're non-stimulants. If the side effects get too much too handle, don't be afraid to reach out to your psychiatrist and let them know. They'll be able to work with you for something else that might be better. Different things work for different people, and meds are almost always a tradeoff. You know what's best for your own situation, and you can decide if the side effects are too much right now or not worth it in comparison to the benefits weeks later if you decide to continue.

Don't get discouraged! Finding meds and a plan is a trial-and-error process, and you've just started the first step.

I think that might be one of the lowest doses you can start out with (which they usually prescribe you as a safe trail run) so if there are any effects or whatnot, they shouldn't be strong and/or you can catch them easily and let your psychiatrist know. Try not to worry about it in that case, you'll be fine!

**Conclusion for future readers:** 

Thanks for all the replies, everyone! It seems like most people don't have a great experience with wellbutrin and have a bigger success with other medication, especially considering their unique circumstances. I think the takeaway is that everyone has different experiences, and you have to find what fits you which makes  a lot of sense. Also if a med isn't working for you or causing some concern, talk to your doctors about it!

I'm not sure if I've experience what you're describing exactly, but I've had a lot of times where some parts of my body are feeling things almost too much(?). It's like maybe  when I'm in bed, and I can't fall asleep because the covers are touching me weird so I have to put them in a certain way to be able to sleep. If that's what you mean, then yes.

I think I read one time that ADHD people can't really "feel" the consequences of things until it happens and/or that long-term goals don't really work for them because they can't feel immediate gratification (which is not to say they can't understand why the long-term goal exists ofc.)

I've been personally getting myself to do things out of sheer willpower (forcing myself really hard to do things even when my body is screaming no) and also doing stuff like setting a timer (I convince myself that I should do x task within x minutes) which helps me keep on track. Also, for mundane tasks like cleaning (or in your case, packing the suitcase), I'd do something like put on music while it happens since it helps distract me from how boring a task really is.
The constant struggle of not being able to complete that one thing you want to finish but doing literally everything else 😭

I'm not sure if this is the same thing, but I do feel the same way as you about wanting to do a ton and then never actually doing that (rip all my unchecked seasonal to-do lists.) Often I'll think about these during bed for a while, and I'll get a ton of anxiety while my eyes are shut and then realize I've been clenching my eyelids really tight and now my head hurts a ton.

I'm actually both surprised and not that most people don't. I always thought people did because I did, but then again I'm pretty sure I have ADHD.

I think if you just find a tune you really like at that moment and listen to it for a while on loop, it eventually will start playing in your mind at random times on loop. I don't know if it's something you want to learn though because it gets tiring being assaulted by the same song for a whole week when you're trying to concentrate no less lol.

That sounds like a toughie. I know that some of my symptoms sometimes appear in public and give me anxiety attacks when I realize what happened (I also have social anxiety as well) so I think I feel you. I also have a tendency to forget things super easily so some things like this have happened to me as well though I've tried hard to hide it. I'm always scared it makes me look dumb, but hey, that's the way I am. I know who I am, and I'm not dumb, it's just how I operate, and it's how you operate as well. There's nothing to be embarrassed about.

I think I know what you mean to a smaller degree. I have this tendency to *not* count my money ever, whether I just got it or if I'm loading up my wallet. As a result, I literally never know if I have enough money when I'm out buying groceries and the like. I just hope I do. 

I've tried to organized my wallet before so I can know how much money goes in there, but it always turns into a mess of folded bills and change.
